name: Cape Verdean Cachupa
description: Cachupa, Cabo Verde's real national dish, is genuinely built on real hominy (alkali-processed corn), not plain corn kernels, simmered slowly with several types of beans together for well over an hour, until the starches released thicken the stew naturally - real versions vary by household, sometimes rich with meat (cachupa rica), sometimes vegetarian (cachupa pobre).

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the paprika and bay leaf, and cook 1 minute.

Add the hominy, cowpeas, sweet potato, and enough water to cover, and simmer 1-1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until everything is very tender and the stew has thickened naturally from the released starches.
Add the cabbage in the last 20 minutes.

name: Cape Verdean Cachupa Refogada
description: Cachupa refogada, leftover cachupa refried the next day and topped with a fried egg, is genuinely its own beloved dish, not just reheated leftovers - a real, essential part of Cape Verdean breakfast culture, especially on weekend mornings.
steps_detailed: Fry the onion in the oil, 3-4 minutes, until golden.
Add the hominy (standing in for leftover cachupa) and fry, pressing and stirring occasionally, 10-12 minutes, until it develops a real golden, slightly crisp crust in spots.
Fry the eggs separately and serve on top - this real refried, egg-topped version is a genuine breakfast dish in its own right.

name: Cape Verdean Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Cabo Verde's deep Atlantic island fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Cape Verdean Feijoada
description: Feijoada, a hearty bean and meat stew, reflects real Portuguese colonial influence found throughout Cabo Verdean cooking - real West African versions of the dish genuinely include carrots, cabbage, and real palm oil, not just beans and meat alone, which was missing here before.

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion in the palm oil, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cowpeas, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and simmer 15-18 minutes more until everything is tender.

name: Cape Verdean Pastel com Diabo Dentro
description: Pastel com diabo dentro, meaning 'pastry with the devil inside', is a real, distinctively named Cape Verdean fried pastry filled with spicy tuna, a beloved snack.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

steps_detailed: Mix the tuna with the onion and jalapeño, being generous with the pepper - the real spicy 'devil' filling that gives the pastry its name.
Fill the phyllo with the mixture and fold into small triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden.

description: A non-alcoholic sugarcane-inspired drink, echoing the flavor of grogue, Cabo Verde's traditional sugarcane spirit, made here as a simple sweetened refresher.
steps_detailed: Dissolve the sugar in 1.5 cups warm water, then stir in the lemon juice and chill before serving over ice.

name: Cape Verdean Fried Fish
description: Simple fried fish, a common Cabo Verdean everyday dish, real technique patting the fish dry first so it fries crisp.
steps_detailed: Pat the fish dry, then dredge in the flour.
Fry, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
